Overall, I have a dedicated and well-equipped home office that meets the standards previously required by my former employer, UnitedHealthcare. As a result, commuting to an office to perform the same work provides little additional value compared to working from my home office. In some situations, it can actually be less efficient. For example, when unexpected or unscheduled calls arise, I can seamlessly manage them from my home workspace. In the office, however, I may need to relocate to find an appropriate space, which can be disruptive and reduce productivity. Given that my home office is already optimized for my work responsibilities, requiring travel to an office environment that offers no meaningful operational advantage feels unnecessary.
Being able print needed information when I go into the office is a plus. Not having access to office supplies while in office makes you have to bring extra stuff when you work in the office.
